proposals.rule: You do not need to wait 12 months to apply if you’re married to a British citizen.
proposals.exception: To apply for citizenship, you must usually have been living in the UK for at least 12 months after being granted indefinite leave.
proposals.why: the general 12-month waiting period after obtaining ILR does not apply to applicants married to a British citizen

proposals.rule: Most people need to pay the immigration health surcharge (IHS) as part of their online immigration application.
proposals.exception: If your course of study is 6 months or less, you do not need to pay the IHS.
proposals.why: covers students with courses of 6 months or less

proposals.rule: Most people need to pay the immigration health surcharge (IHS) as part of their online immigration application.
proposals.exception: In line with our longstanding commitments under the Common Travel Area, Irish citizens will not be subject to the immigration health surcharge.
proposals.why: Irish citizens are exempt from the surcharge

proposals.rule: You’ll still need to pay for certain types of services, such as prescriptions, dental treatment, eye tests and assisted conception.
proposals.exception: If you give birth to a child in the UK, your child will be entitled to free NHS hospital treatment in England on the same basis as someone who is ordinarily resident.
proposals.why: Children born in the UK to eligible parents are entitled to free hospital treatment

proposals.rule: Most people need to pay the immigration health surcharge (IHS) as part of their online immigration application.
proposals.exception: If you’re eligible to apply for the Health and Care visa, you will also be exempt from having to pay the Immigration Health Surcharge.
proposals.why: applies to applicants for the Health and Care visa

proposals.exception: You do not need to pay the immigration health surcharge or biometric enrolment fee.
